summary: Buffington Harbor Breakwater light: a red concrete tower on a private breakwater at Gary, Indiana, built for a cement harbor and opened in 1927.

structures.type: round concrete tower on fog-signal structure
structures.note: Rowlett: 46 ft (14 m) tower; Pepper: 50-ft shaft on a 30-ft base; Rowlett dates the light to 1926, Pepper to early 1927; 13-mile visibility (the sources do not say statute or nautical miles)

access.note: Private breakwater; accessible only by boat; site and tower closed (Rowlett). Not open to the public (USLHS).

facts.agency: City of Gary (owner); Gary New Century LLC (site manager), per Rowlett

events.note: Gas buoy established at Buffington Harbor, reported under the heading for July 1925 (Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1925, PDF p. 32; checked on the page image)
Rowlett gives 1926 for the light; Pepper dates the east-pier acetylene light to 1 November 1926 and the concrete light to early 1927
Concrete light structure built on a sheet-piling base, early 1927 (Pepper)
Harbor opened 10 June 1927 with Vice President Charles G. Dawes (LighthouseFriends, Pepper); the Indianapolis Times reports the opening as on Thursday
Part of the cement plant property sold for casino development; two floating casinos in the harbor
Remaining plant property sold to the City of Gary for $25 million

corrections.proposed: City of Gary (owner); Gary New Century LLC (site manager)
corrections.why: Rowlett and LighthouseFriends name the City of Gary as owner. Pepper calls the breakwater private property; see resolved conflicts.
Rowlett: accessible only by boat, site and tower closed; USLHS: not open to the public.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett dates the light to 1926. Pepper dates the east-pier acetylene light to 1 November 1926 and the concrete breakwater light to early 1927. The story gives early 1927 for the concrete light and Rowlett's 1926 as a difference.
LighthouseFriends and Pepper give 10 June 1927. The Indianapolis Times of 10 June says Dawes formally opened the harbor on Thursday (9 June). Unresolved; the story reports both.
Pepper: sixteen guns. Indianapolis Times: nineteen guns. Unresolved.
Pepper: sixty acres. LighthouseFriends: fifty-five acres. Unresolved.
Pepper: most of the harbor was sold. LighthouseFriends: one-third of the Buffington property was sold. Both agree on two floating casinos.
Rowlett and LighthouseFriends: City of Gary owns the light. Pepper: breakwater and light are private property. Possibly both true (city owns, private breakwater); unresolved.
Rowlett: 46 ft (14 m) round concrete tower. Pepper: 50-ft shaft on a 30-ft base. Possibly different measures (the shaft versus the tower to the lantern); unresolved.

notes_for_editor: Position: the record's coordinates (41.646039, -87.410323) agree with LighthouseFriends (41.64605, -87.41032) and with Pepper (41 deg 38' 45.55" N, 87 deg 24' 37.28" W); no correction. Name: the USLHS archive calls the record 'Buffington Harbor East Breakwater' and types it as a minor aid to navigation, with no roster; its coordinates are unusable (latitude 41 deg 64.60 min is not a valid minute value; read as decimal degrees, the record's point is about 50 km from the light). Federal establishment: no Lighthouse Service Bulletin in the corpus names the breakwater light as established; the 1925 Bulletin lists only a gas buoy at Buffington Harbor. The 1926/1927 dates are therefore from Pepper, LighthouseFriends and Rowlett, not from the official record. The Gary Post-Tribune items cited by LighthouseFriends (9-10 June 1927, and a 1939 Universal Atlas program) were not read. Pepper's copyright notice: facts only. Keepers: none named in any source read; the record does not say whether the light is staffed; do not assume. Storms and rescues: none in the sources read. The record's arlhs 'USA-101' is a truncation of Rowlett's 'USA-1017'. The breakwater light has only the 'Fl R 4s' characteristic from the record (ENC); Rowlett gives 'red flash every 4 s', consistent. RANGE: the sources give 13 miles (LighthouseFriends, Pepper) without saying whether nautical; the guide asks for nautical miles, so confirm or convert before publication. Fact-check 2026-10-28: Pepper (cite 2), LighthouseFriends (cite 3), Rowlett (cite 1), the Indianapolis Times page 8 (cite 4) and the 1925 Bulletin PDF p. 32 (cite 5) were re-read. The Thursday opening, the nineteen-gun and sixteen-gun salutes, the 1925 gas buoy and the 2000 sale were confirmed. The story now dates the light to 1926 or 1927 (Rowlett 1926; Pepper early 1927) instead of 1927 alone, states the height disagreement (Rowlett 46 ft tower; Pepper 50 ft shaft), and cites LighthouseFriends for best seen from the water. The USLHS Buffington Harbor East Breakwater record (cite 6) is a Minor Aid to Navigation matched by name only, with invalid printed coordinates, so it is used only for not open to the public, with that caveat. Pepper's virtually impossible to see from the land is now quoted, and the disagreement on views from land is stated. Sentences that followed Pepper or LighthouseFriends wording closely were rewritten.
